Poroshkovo Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Zakarpattia Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Jews are believed to have arrived in Poroshkovo in the 19th century, growing from 21 people in 1851 to 130 by 1910, before declining to 94 by 1930 under Czechoslovakian rule. This cemetery, with separate sections for men and women, presumably emerged in the 19th century, already existing by 1906. Following the Hungarian occupation of March 1939, Jews were persecuted and forced out of their occupations; some were drafted into forced labor battalions or sent to the Eastern Front, where most perished. Jews without Hungarian citizenship were expelled to Kamianets-Podilskyi in Nazi-occupied Ukraine and murdered, and the remaining Jews of Poroshkovo were deported to Auschwitz in late May 1944.
